algorithms.html: A DID resolver implements the following DID resolution algorithm.

steps.html: Validate that the input DID conforms to the did rule of the DID Syntax. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the DID method of the input DID is supported by the DID resolver that implements this algorithm. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the input DID resolution options are supported by the DID resolver that implements this algorithm. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the input DID resolution options are valid. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_OPTIONS
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Obtain the DID document for the input DID by executing the Resolve operation, as defined by the input DID method:
If the input DID does not exist, return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
If the input DID has been deactivated, return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: «[ ... ]»
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ "deactivated" → true, ... ]»
Otherwise, the result of the Resolve operation is called the output DID document. This result MUST be represented in a conformant representation.
If the input DID resolution options contain the expandRelativeUrls option with a value of true:
Iterate over all services, verification methods, verification relationships and any extension-defined properties in the output DID document.
For each item, if the item is an object and the value of the id property is a relative DID URL, or if a verification relationship is a relative DID URL:
Resolve the relative DID URL to an absolute DID URL conformant with DID URL Syntax, according to the rules of section Relative DID URLs in Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0.
Update the output DID document by replacing the relative DID URLs with the resolved absolute DID URLs.
Return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: «[ ... ]»
didDocument: output DID document
didDocumentMetadata: «[ "contentType" → output DID document media type, ... ]»

algorithms.html: If the DID resolver encounters any unexpected errors during the execution of the DID Resolution algorithm, it MUST return the following result:

steps.html: didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INTERNAL_ERROR
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Validate that the input DID URL conforms to the did-url rule of the DID URL Syntax. If not, the DID URL dereferencer MUST return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_URL
contentStream: null
contentMetadata: «[ ]»

Obtain the DID document for the input DID by executing the DID resolution algorithm as defined in 4. DID Resolution. All dereferencing options and all DID parameters of the input DID URL MUST be passed as resolution options to the DID Resolution algorithm.
If the input DID does not exist in the VDR, the DID URL dereferencer MUST return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND
contentStream: null
contentMetadata: «[ ]»
Otherwise, the didDocument result of the DID resolution algorithm is called the resolved DID document.
If present, separate the DID fragment from the input DID URL and continue with the adjusted input DID URL.
If the input DID URL contains no DID path and no DID query: The DID URL dereferencer MUST return the resolved DID document and resolved 4.3 DID Document Metadata as follows:
dereferencingMetadata: «[ ... ]»
contentStream: resolved DID document
contentMetadata: «[ resolved DID document metadata ]»
If the input DID URL contains the DID parameter service and/or the DID parameter serviceType, and optionally the DID parameter relativeRef:
From the resolved DID document, select all services which fulfill the following conditions:

If the input DID URL contains the DID parameter service: Select the service if its id property matches the value of the service DID parameter. If the id property or the service DID parameter or both contain relative references, the corresponding absolute URIs MUST be resolved and used for determining the match, using the rules specified in RFC3986 Section 5: Reference Resolution and in section Relative DID URLs in Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0.
If the input DID URL contains the DID parameter serviceType: Select the service if its type property matches the value of the serviceType DID parameter.
If the input DID URL contains the DID parameter relativeRef:
For each selected service:
If the value of the serviceEndpoint property of the selected service is a map, skip this selected service.
If the value of the serviceEndpoint property of the selected service is a string, add this value to a list of selected DID service endpoint URLs.
If the value of the serviceEndpoint property of the selected service is a set, add all its items that are strings to a list of selected DID service endpoint URLs.

Dereferencing a DID service endpoint — particularly one that is a DID — might result in a dereferencing cycle, which is a set of steps that result in an infinite loop. For example, a DID service endpoint might indirectly point back through a sequence of dereferencing processes to a previously dereferenced identifier. A DID URL dereferencer recursively dereferencing a DID service endpoint is advised to detect and handle such a cycle to prevent an infinite loop or dereferencing failure. For further guidance, see Section Dereferencing Cycles.
The base URI value is the selected DID service endpoint URL.
The relative reference is the value of the DID parameter relativeRef.
Update the selected DID service endpoint URL to the result of the "Reference Resolution" algorithm.
If the accept input DID URL dereferencing option is missing, or if its value is the Media Type of a representation of a DID document:
Update the services in the resolved DID document to contain only the selected services.
Return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: «[ ... ]»
content: resolved DID document with selected services
contentMetadata: «[ resolved DID document metadata ]»
If the value of the accept input DID URL deferencing option is text/uri-list:
Return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: «[ ... ]»
content: « selected service endpoint URLs »
contentMetadata: «[ "contentType" → "text/uri-list", ... ]»
Otherwise, return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#REPRESENTATION_NOT_SUPPORTED
content: null
contentMetadata: «[ ]»
Otherwise, if the input DID URL contains a DID path and/or DID query:
The applicable DID method MAY specify how to dereference the DID path and/or DID query of the input DID URL.
An extension specification MAY specify how to dereference the DID path of the input DID URL.
An extension specification MAY specify how to dereference the DID query of the input DID URL.
The client MAY be able to dereference the input DID URL in an application-specific way.
If neither this algorithm, nor the applicable DID method, nor an extension, nor the client is able to dereference the input DID URL, return the following result:
dereferencingMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND
contentStream: null
contentMetadata: «[ ]»

algorithms.html: If the input DID URL contains a DID fragment, then dereferencing of the fragment is dependent on the media type ([RFC2046]) of the resource, i.e., on the result of 5.4.1 Dereferencing the Resource.

steps.html: If the result of 5.4.1 Dereferencing the Resource is an output DID document, and the input DID URL dereferencing options contain the verificationRelationship option:
Let verificationRelationship be the value of the verificationRelationship option.
Let verificationMethod be the result of dereferencing the DID fragment from the output DID document according to the rules of the media type of the DID document.
If verificationMethod is not a conforming verification method, an error MUST be raised and SHOULD convey an error type of INVALID_VERIFICATION_METHOD.

If verificationMethod is not associated, either by reference (URL) or by value (object), with the verification relationship array in the output DID document identified by verificationRelationship, an error MUST be raised and SHOULD convey an error type of INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_FOR_VERIFICATION_METHOD.
Return the <var>verificationMethod</var>.
If the result of 5.4.1 Dereferencing the Resource is a selected DID service endpoint URL, and the input DID URL contains a DID fragment:
If the selected DID service endpoint URL contains a fragment component, raise an error.
Append the DID fragment to the select DID service endpoint URL. In other words, the select DID service endpoint URL "inherits" the DID fragment of the input DID URL.
Return the select DID service endpoint URL.

Otherwise, dereference the DID fragment as defined by the media type ([RFC2046]) of the resource. For example, if the resource is a representation of a DID document with media type application/did, then the fragment is treated according to the rules associated with the JSON-LD 1.1: application/ld+json media type [JSON-LD11].
Prepare for Resolution
Resolve the DID
Determine Handling Strategy
Invoke the Handler
Use the Handler Result

Validate that the input DID URL conforms to the did-url rule of the DID URL Syntax. If not, the DID URL client MUST end without further processing, indicating a failure due to an https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_URL

Select a resolver that is capable of handling the DID's method. Implementers MUST enable users to choose the resolvers they trust for specific DID methods. It is expected that implementations will provide this through some configuration mechanism, the details of which are out of scope for this specification.
Extract the DID from the DID URL, e.g., the DID URL did:ex:abc#key-1 contains the DID did:ex:abc.

Prepare DID resolution options. These may be promoted from DID URL query parameters or determined by the business rules of the context in which the DID URL is being dereferenced. It is the business context in which the client is executing the algorithm that determines whether or not any given query parameter should be promoted to a Resolution option. See the resolving algorithm for details about resolution options and their meaning.
Call the resolve function on the selected resolver, passing the prepared resolution options and the DID, to obtain the authoritative DID document for the input DID URL.

Interpret the response to resolve to consider any errors or warnings. If appropriate, return without further processing and raise a DEREFERENCING_ERROR_RESOLUTION_ERROR that includes he error returned from the Resolve Operation. Otherwise, continue processing if the response provided enough information to do so.

Repeat as necessary until the final resolution result is returned. In cases when the initial result from resolution is incomplete or fails, the client may be able to adjust the resolution parameters and try again, based on the context in which dereferencing is occuring. For example, a resolver might require more input, or the client might heuristically attempt alternate resolver options to find a more appropriate DID document, such as requesting a version of the DID document from a particular point in time.

algorithms.html: Using the result from resolution, execute the following steps starting with the Services Step until a handling strategy is determined. End processing as soon as a strategy is set.

steps.html:
Services Step

If service is present as a DID query Parameter, first check whether multiple service parameters are present in the DID URL. If there are, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SERVICE_PARAMETERS and continue to the Default DID Document step. If there is just one service parameter, use the service selection algorithm to select the appropriate service object. Then, if there is no matching service object, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If the selected object's service type has defined a handling strategy, set the strategy to that. If the service type does not define a handling strategy, set strategy to the Default Service Handler Strategy. Otherwise, continue with the PathHandlers Step.

PathHandlers Step

If the DID URL contains a non-empty path part, then use the PathHandler Path Matching Algorithm to select a path handler object. If no path handler objects are selected, continue to the Document Properties step. If there are multiple handler objects selected, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_MATCHING_PATH_HANDLERS and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If the sole selected path handling object has a secondary type that defines a handler strategy, set the strategy to that strategy. If it doesn't, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_PATH_HANDLER_HANDLER_NOT_DEFINED and continue to the Default DID Document Step.

Document Properties Step

If the DID document contains any properties known to define a handler strategy, check whether any of those properties apply to the DID URL. If not, continue with the Method-Specific Step. If the DID document contains multiple properties that apply to the DID URL, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_DOCUMENT_PROPERTIES and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If the DID document contains a single property with a known handler strategy that applies to the DID URL, set the strategy to the strategy defined by that property. Otherwise, continue to the Method-Specific Step.

Method-Specific Step

If the DID method defines a method-specific handler strategy, check whether that handler applies to the DID URL. If it does, set the handler strategy to that specified by the DID method. If there is no applicable method-specific handler strategy, continue with the Query Parameters Step.

Query Parameters Step

If there are query parameters that require a specific handling strategy, check to see if there are more than one. If there are, then raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_QUERY_PARAMETERS and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If there is only one such query parameter, set the strategy to that defined by the query parameter specification. Otherwise, continue with the Metadata Step.

Not all query parameters will change the handling strategy. For example, versionTime and versionId only change the resolution result, but do not impact the dereferencing step.

Metadata Step

If either the DID resolution metadata or DID document metadata contain any properties known to define a handler strategy, check to see if any of those properties apply to the DID URL. If there is only one such property, set the strategy to the strategy defined by that property. If there are multiple applicable properties, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_METADATA_PROPERTIES and continue to the Default DID Document Step. Otherwise, continue to Default DID Document Step.
Default DID Document Step If no other handler strategy has been determined, set the strategy to Return DID Document.

Execute the determined handler strategy using a handler that implements that strategy. If the client does not have a handler that implements the determined strategy, stop processing and raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_HANDLER_NOT_FOUND.

algorithms.html: When a DID URL contains a service parameter use the following algorithm to determine which service should be used for dereferencing the DID URL.

steps.html: Select the service from the DID document whose id property matches the value of the service DID query parameter. If either the id property or the service DID parameter or both contain relative references, the corresponding absolute URIs MUST be computed and used for determining the match, using the rules specified in RFC3986 Section 5: Reference Resolution and in section Relative DID URLs in Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0.
If a single service matches, that service is selected. Continue with the Services Step.

Select Service Endpoint If serviceEndpoint is a single value, use it. If serviceEndpoint is instead an array, randomly pick one of the service's serviceEndpoint values as a starting point. Since each value in the array is expected to resolve to the same set of resources (and any given DID URL triggering that service will retrieve the same resource from any of the endpoints), successfully dreferencing any one of them is sufficient. Implementations MUST keep track of each endpoint as it is attempted, so that each is exercised until either a successful result is returned or the complete set of endpoints has been attempted. In other words raise a failure error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_NO_SERVICE_ENDPOINTS_SUCCEED only after all of the endpoints fail. 
serviceEndpoint = "https://example.com/didimages/"

Determine Resource Path Construct the resource path by extracting the non-matching part of the DID URL and appending it to the path of the serviceEndpoint. First extract the non-matching part of the DID URL path as the pathExtension. The pathExtension in the above example is "image.png", after stripping the service's path value of "/" from the path part of the DID URL /image.png. 
pathExtension = "image.png";
 Append the pathExtension to the path part of the serviceEndpoint to define the resourchPath. 
resourcePath = /didimages/image.png

Normalize Path Normalize the resulting ResourcePath to create a NormalizedResourcePath by removing dot segments, as defined in [RFC3986] Section 5.2.4 Remove Path Segments. Then test the resulting NormalizedResourcePath to see if the leftmost characters of the NormalizedResourcePath match the leftmost characters of the path part of the serviceEndpoint. If they do not match, raise an error DEREFERENCE_ERROR_PATH_NORMALIZATION_ERROR.

Construct Resource URLs Replace the path part in the selected serviceEndpoint with the Normalized Resource Path, leaving all other elements of the service endpoint URLs the same. 
ResourceUrl = https://example.com/didimages/image.png
Dereference Resource URL Dereference the resulting ResourceUrl according to its scheme. For example, for an https URL, perform a GET operation on that URL.

algorithms.html: When a DID Document contains a path and one or more objects with a type of PathHandler use the following algorithm to determine which object and handler should be used for dereferencing the DID URL.

steps.html:
Of those objects with a type PathHandler, select the object whose path property has the longest complete match from the beginning of the path part of the DID URL. The entire value of the path property must be present in the path part of the DID URL.
Given the DID URL did:example:1234/image.png and the following three PathHandling objects

In this scenario, the linkedResource with id SecuredImage would be selected and it's handling strategy would be defined by the LinkedResource specification.
If two or more objects have the same length match, stop processing and return an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_MATCHING_PATH_HANDLERS.

algorithms.html: Using this binding, the DID resolution function (see 4. DID Resolution) and/or DID URL dereferencing function (see 5. DID URL Dereferencing) can be executed as follows:

steps.html: Initialize a request HTTP(S) URL with the DID resolver HTTP(S) endpoint.
For the DID resolution function:
Append the input DID to the request HTTP(S) URL.
Set the Accept HTTP request header to application/did-resolution to request a complete 9. DID Resolution Result, OR
set the Accept HTTP request header to the value of the accept resolution option to request only the didDocument value of the result.
For the DID URL dereferencing function:
Append the input DID URL to the request HTTP(S) URL.
Set the Accept HTTP request header to application/did-url-dereferencing to request a complete 10. DID URL Dereferencing Result, OR
set the Accept HTTP request header to the value of the accept dereferencing option to request only the contentStream value of the result.
For the HTTP(S) GET binding:
If any other resolution options or dereferencing options than accept are provided:
The input DID MUST be URL-encoded (as specified in RFC3986 Section 2.1).
Encode all resolution options except accept as query parameters in the request HTTP(S) URL.
Execute an HTTP GET request on the request HTTP(S) URL. This invokes the DID resolution or DID URL dereferencing function at the remote DID resolver.
For the HTTP(S) POST binding:
If any other resolution options or dereferencing options than accept are provided:
Encode all resolution options except accept as a JSON structure in the HTTP request's POST body.
Execute an HTTP POST request on the request HTTP(S) URL. This invokes the DID resolution or DID URL dereferencing function at the remote DID resolver.

If the DID resolution or DID URL dereferencing function returns an error metadata property in the didResolutionMetadata or dereferencingMetadata, then the HTTP response status code MUST correspond to the type property of the error object, according to the following table:
error type URI HTTP status code
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_URL 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_OPTIONS 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND 404
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#REPRESENTATION_NOT_SUPPORTED 406
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_DOCUMENT 500
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED 501
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED 501
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INTERNAL_ERROR 500

If the type property of the error object does not appear in the table above, then the HTTP response status code is determined by the implementation.
If the DID resolution or DID URL dereferencing function returns a deactivated metadata property with the value true in the didDocumentMetadata or contentMetadata:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 410.
For the DID resolution function:
If the value of the Content-Type HTTP response header is application/did-resolution:
The HTTP body MUST contain a DID resolution result (see 9. DID Resolution Result) that is the result of the DID resolution function.
If the function is successful and returns a didDocument:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 200.
The HTTP response MUST contain a Content-Type HTTP response header. Its value MUST be the value of the contentType metadata property in the didResolutionMetadata (see 4.2 DID Resolution Metadata).
The HTTP response body MUST contain the didDocument that is the result of the DID resolution function, in the representation corresponding to the Content-Type HTTP response header.
For the DID URL dereferencing function:
If the value of the Content-Type HTTP response header is application/did-url-dereferencing:
The HTTP body MUST contain a DID URL dereferencing result (see 10. DID URL Dereferencing Result) that is the result of the DID URL dereferencing function.
If the function is successful and returns a contentStream and a contentType metadata property with the value text/uri-list in the dereferencingMetadata:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 303.
The HTTP response MUST contain an Location header. The value of this header MUST be the selected DID service endpoint URL.
the HTTP response body MUST be empty.
If the function is successful and returns a contentStream with any other contentType:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 200.

The HTTP response MUST contain a Content-Type HTTP response header. Its value MUST be the value of the contentType metadata property in the dereferencingMetadata (see 5.2 DID URL Dereferencing Metadata).
The HTTP response body MUST contain the contentStream that is the result of the DID URL dereferencing function, in the representation corresponding to the Content-Type HTTP response header.
